_about: Machine-readable seed ledger for Rosetta vNext. It implements the theoretical contract in 03_ROSETTA_VNEXT_THEORETICAL_CONTRACT.md and the audit fields in 10_CELL_AUDIT_SCHEMA_2026_04_25.md.
This is a seed, not the corpus. It retains the four original teleology and ontology collision examples while migrating them into directional, versioned projection claims.

PHIL7@1 places the purpose question first while GEN7@1 places a teleology analogy at L7. PHIL7@1 places being/ontology sixth while GEN7@1 places an ontology analogy at L5. Those are data about two packs, not a license for bare Lx claims.
A changed meaning creates a new pack version or cell revision. Failed and superseded revisions remain present; the checker rejects dangling, reciprocal, cyclic, or in-place status rewrites.

packs.description: Seven selected philosophical questions used as a reversible navigation prototype.
packs.target_domain: declared independently by each directional cell
semantic_normalization: trim and collapse whitespace within each non-empty line
packs.proposed_invariant: The identities and selected order of seven questions remain recognizable as a non-causal navigation interface.
discarded_information: workflow orders other than the selected reading order
packs.strongest_rival: A domain-native philosophical taxonomy with a different count or order is equally or more usable without Rosetta notation.
packs.discriminator: In a blinded comparison, independent readers apply this index with fewer omissions or equivocations than named rival indexes without inferring causal order or hierarchy.
packs.kill_criterion: Retire or contract the pack if its seven selected prompts repeatedly force overlap, hierarchy, or worse decisions than a simpler rival index.

must_report_as_loss: any order introduced only by the target

revision_event.reason: Register the active question index under a versioned namespace.

packs.description: Seven interface seats in the selected generative cross-domain catalogue.
packs.target_domain: declared independently by each directional cell
semantic_normalization: trim and collapse whitespace within each non-empty line

normalization_operations.detail: Select seven interface seats from several traditions whose native cardinalities and category boundaries differ.
normalization_operations.destroyed_information: Domain-native counts, alternate members, and within-domain disagreements are not represented by the row key.

normalization_operations.detail: Render source-domain terms as compact historical-social, inferential, philosophical, and mathematical analogies.
normalization_operations.destroyed_information: Native vocabulary, context, causal direction, and scale are compressed.

packs.proposed_invariant: A selected boundary-to-horizon reading order remains legible across explicitly interpretive columns without transferring proof between them.
packs.strongest_rival: The apparent seven-row fit is produced by flexible selection and framework-derived labels rather than a shared cross-domain structure.
packs.discriminator: Independent coders using frozen source material and held-out cells prefer the preregistered GEN7 placements over cheaper rival maps without post-hoc relabeling.
packs.kill_criterion: Kill or contract the cross-domain pack when held-out material fits rivals equally well, native counts must be hidden, or post-hoc relabeling rescues every failure.

must_report_as_loss: causal and normative information not carried by the analogy

revision_event.reason: Register the selected generative catalogue under a versioned namespace while declaring its normalization loss.

cells.domain_expression: Teleology — what end or purpose is being proposed?
cells.fit_reason: Both terms use teleological vocabulary, but PHIL7 asks a cross-cutting purpose question while GEN7 places an ultimate-horizon analogy in its final seat.
discarded_information: the difference between a cross-cutting question and a row analogy
all implications of the incompatible local row numbers
cells.strongest_rival: The shared word is lexical coincidence or framework reuse and carries no stable mapping.
cells.discriminator: Independent coders distinguish the shared invariant from the omitted differences using frozen definitions and a preregistered coding guide.
cells.kill_criterion: Killed as a bare-row identity already: PHIL7@1:purpose and GEN7@1:L7 carry maximally different local positions. Kill the namespaced analogy too if coders cannot identify an invariant beyond the shared word.
cells.downgrade_path: Retain the collision record, set fit_status to KILLED in this revision, and create a new revision only for a materially different relation.

revision_event.reason: Preserve the teleology collision as a directional, namespaced v2 claim.

cells.fit_reason: GEN7's final-seat horizon analogy may be interrogated by PHIL7's purpose question, but the inverse direction is a fresh claim rather than an automatic inverse.
discarded_information: whether transcendental, teleological, and theocratic language share a single source-domain function
the cross-cutting character of PHIL7 questions
cells.strongest_rival: GEN7's teleology label is a decorative final-seat analogy with no reproducible relation to PHIL7's purpose question.
cells.discriminator: Held-out GEN7 examples are classified more reliably by the purpose prompt than by rival PHIL7 prompts under a frozen coding guide.
cells.kill_criterion: The bare claim 'L7 is teleology' is already killed across packs. Kill this directional analogy if held-out examples do not discriminate purpose from rival prompts.
cells.downgrade_path: Retain the failed revision and supersede it only with a narrower, receipt-backed claim.

revision_event.reason: Preserve the reverse teleology comparison without treating direction as invertible.

cells.domain_expression: Ontology — what kinds of entities or relations are posited?
cells.fit_reason: Both terms use ontology vocabulary, while PHIL7 treats it as a cross-cutting entity-and-relation audit and GEN7 uses it in an architecture seat.
discarded_information: the difference between a question and an architectural analogy
cells.strongest_rival: The shared word masks two non-equivalent uses and supplies no cross-pack invariant.
cells.discriminator: Independent coders can state and recover a non-lexical invariant while also naming the lost distinctions.
cells.kill_criterion: The bare ontology row claim is already killed because PHIL7@1:being and GEN7@1:L5 occupy different local positions. Kill the analogy if no invariant survives removal of the shared label.
cells.downgrade_path: Retain the collision record and replace ontology identity with a narrower entity-audit or architecture relation in a new revision.

revision_event.reason: Preserve the ontology collision as a directional, namespaced v2 claim.

cells.fit_reason: An architecture row can be interrogated for its entity and relation commitments, but that does not make systematic philosophy, ontology, and aristocracy synonyms.
discarded_information: differences among systematic philosophy, ontology, and political analogy
other PHIL7 questions that can interrogate the same row
cells.strongest_rival: The PHIL7 being prompt is no more informative for GEN7's architecture row than several other prompts.
cells.discriminator: A held-out audit finds preregistered entity-boundary errors at GEN7@1:L5 that rival prompts fail to detect under matched effort.
cells.kill_criterion: Kill the directional analogy if the being prompt does not outperform rival prompts or if the result depends only on the preselected ontology label.
cells.downgrade_path: Retain the failed revision and supersede only with a narrower, discriminated relation.

revision_event.reason: Preserve the reverse ontology comparison without treating direction as invertible.
